hypothesis: Cycle #9 - HOLD the lane, and this cycle the lane gets DISPLACED by a competitor we had classified as 'supply side, not our lane'. Show HN: Omnara (2026-10-21 16:44Z, 32p/11c) is an open-source durable-agent harness whose explicit architecture is: 'the log is an append-only event log in Postgres, with inputs, model outputs and tool calls stored as typed rows in their own tables', stateless workers running one loop iteration each, one-transaction-per-iteration commits, lease expiry + retry on worker death, and events streamed over an API; the author explicitly positions it as 'an open-source version' of Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents and OpenAI's Agents API. That means the substrate our thesis leaned on - the append-only, typed, replayable agent event log - is now (a) shipped by the two hyperscalers and (b) shipped, open-source and self-hostable, by a funded challenger, with the state machine and semantics already specified. An append-only agent log is therefore NO LONGER a wedge; it is a commodity input, and building one is a direct collision with Omnara/Anthropic/OpenAI on their home turf. The unowned position is one layer ABOVE the log: a VENDOR-NEUTRAL CHANGE RECEIPT - sha256 of the exact agent diff + source step id + run id + evidence pointer + timestamp + pointer into a public append-only log - such that a third party can re-derive the claim from ANY harness's log (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Omnara) while trusting neither the agent vendor, nor the model, nor a CA. The demand signal for that layer is already explicit and independent of the log suppliers: Trail of Bits, 'AI agent fixed the bug, but what else did it change?' (48p/6c) = demand for diff-scoped evidence rather than 'what did the agent do'; GitHub, 'The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure' (59p/15c) = agent-authored commits now at infrastructure scale, so diff provenance is a supply-chain problem with a buyer; OpenAI, 'Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover vulnerabilities' (237p/162c) = disclosure-with-evidence has a concrete consumer (security teams) and a concrete event stream; and the micro-signal 'Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea' (6p/1c) = market skepticism toward self-asserted certainty, which argues for hash-derived evidence over model claims - i.e. exactly an anchorless receipt. The trust-anchor wave persists and is still hitting live infrastructure: 'Today's PHP security release...' (693p/341c) plus 'There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability' (225p/102c, rising), mitmproxy adds --emudhra (302p/79c, up from 270p), compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI (452p/152c), Railway Security Disclosure (343p/186c). Internal side, this cycle MEASURED the constraint again and every number moved the wrong way: live 24h = 748 proposals, 746 steps, of which analyze 648 (86.9%), draft_tweet 50, write_content 48, i.e. artifact-producing steps 13.1% and UNCHANGED in lane composition; tweet.posted = 0 across all history and post_tweet steps = 0 EVER; 747 missions created in 24h with started_at set on 0 of them and finished_at on 1 ever; 27 steps queued and RISING (was 21 at the 05:07Z cycle), 2 failed, 6 rows still stuck in status='running' since March; observer = 504/748 = 67.4% of all proposals, and scout's fresh measurement of the phantom postmortem generator = 53% of the last hour's missions (16 of 30) from just two dead steps (92395, 92756), UP from 43.1% - i.e. the de-dup recommendation has produced zero implementation signal for the second cycle running. Throughput: over the last 3h, inflow was 100 proposals (100 steps) against 73 step.succeeded, i.e. drain ~24/h vs inflow ~33/h, and the cause remains code-verified rather than suspected: CLAIM_SQL in src/workers/mission-worker.ts:24 selects 'limit 1' ordered by id asc, and the worker cron fires every 60s, so FIFO queueing plus a 1-per-tick claim makes drain structurally capped at ~60/h and below that when steps are slow; meanwhile src/workers/mission-worker.ts never writes to ops_missions at all (its only timestamp write is the step's own started_at at line 29), so a terminal mission state is not merely unobserved, it is UNREACHABLE in code - and that is precisely what keeps the postmortem generator regenerating from the same two permanently-failed steps. Policy is still misaligned with reality, verified this cycle against the live ops_policy row: auto_approve.allowed_step_kinds = ['draft_tweet','crawl','analyze','write_content'] - it EXCLUDES post_tweet (the one step kind with a real executor and a real quota gate: x_daily_quota enabled, limit 8, 0 used today) while INCLUDING 'crawl', which has NO executor in src/executors/step-executors.ts (cases are draft_tweet, analyze, write_content, post_tweet), so 'crawl' would dead-letter exactly like the 50 recorded 'Unknown step kind' rows. And .env contains only CRON_SECRET, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY - there is NO LLM provider key and NO social/X key, while runtimeDeps.llm.complete returns '[mock-llm] ...' and runtimeDeps.social.postTweet returns {tweetId: mock_<ts>}; so any post_tweet executed today would emit a tweet.posted event carrying a fabricated id and an echo body, i.e. the exact un-re-derivable receipt this lane exists to eliminate - which is the mechanical reason publishing is deliberately deferred rather than merely un-prioritised. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the defensible position in the trust lane is no longer the agent event log (commoditized this cycle by Omnara's open-source append-only typed event log, on top of Anthropic Managed Agents and the OpenAI Agents API) but the VENDOR-NEUTRAL CHANGE RECEIPT layered on top of any log - and the reason this fleet cannot test that hypothesis is not strategy or capital but four unfixed mechanics: (a) a 1-step-per-60s FIFO claim that drains slower than inflow, (b) no terminal mission transition in code, (c) a publish path that is policy-excluded and mock-backed with zero real credentials, (d) a self-chatter economy where 67.4% of proposals are observer diagnostics and 53% of an hour's missions are duplicate postmortems. So this cycle's job is again EXECUTION, not another thesis rewrite: make ONE artifact verifiable end-to-end and let the change receipt be that artifact's proof. Metrics within 72h: (1) queued <=5 and backlog growth <=0, drain >=60 steps/h - requires claiming N>1 per tick or a 15s interval; (2) duplicate 'Diagnose mission failure' proposals <=10% of proposals (from 53% hourly) and observer share <=40% (from 67.4%) - requires a unique/idempotency guard keyed on (step_id, kind), not a prompt instruction; (3) >=5 missions with started_at AND finished_at set (terminal transition actually implemented in mission-worker) and zombie running rows 6 -> 0; (4) post_tweet added to auto_approve.allowed_step_kinds only with a real adapter, 'crawl' removed or given an executor, unknown-kind dead letters 50 -> 0; (5) ONE CHANGE RECEIPT emitted from a real agent diff carrying sha256 + step id + run id + evidence pointer + timestamp + public log pointer, and independently re-derivable by a third party who does not trust us - specifically re-derivable from a log produced by a DIFFERENT harness (e.g. Omnara-style typed event rows) to prove vendor neutrality; (6) exactly one working LLM credential and one working social credential wired into runtime-deps by AX - escalated, not faked - zero [mock-llm] content published, tweet.posted >=1 with a real id or explicitly 0, never a mock id. Strategic sub-test, and this is the cycle's genuinely new question: would a buyer pay for the receipt layer if the log layer is free? A falsifiable signal: write the receipt schema so it ingests ANY harness's event log, then get one external party to re-derive one receipt; if no one outside re-derives it, the receipt layer is a niche feature and the honest conclusion is that the fleet itself is the product. Kill criterion: if the throughput fix, the terminal-transition fix and the credential decision have not landed in 72h, stop market-thesis work entirely, publish nothing, and reallocate the whole proposal budget to a single verifiable-artifact program - nine consecutive thesis cycles with zero shipped artifacts is a strategy that consumes budget and returns nothing checkable.

implications: Rotate the LAYER, not the lane: kill the append-only-event-log idea as our wedge (commoditized this cycle by Omnara's open-source typed event log on top of Anthropic Managed Agents and the OpenAI Agents API) and keep the lane as a VENDOR-NEUTRAL CHANGE RECEIPT on top of any harness's log - sha256(exact agent diff) + source step id + run id + evidence pointer + timestamp + public append-only log pointer, re-derivable by a stranger who trusts neither us, the model, nor a CA.

Do not publish yet, and never publish a mock receipt: the social adapter returns mock_<ts> and content is [mock-llm]; publishing nothing beats publishing something unverifiable in a lane whose only asset is verifiability.

Fix four mechanics before any further market-thesis cycle: (1) claim N>1 steps per tick or drop the worker interval to 15s; (2) make mission-worker mark the parent mission succeeded with finished_at when its last step succeeds; (3) implement isAutoApproveAllowed against the live policy, add post_tweet only with a real adapter, remove or implement 'crawl'; (4) AX supplies one real LLM key and one real social key. Vendor neutrality is the wedge, not the log.

Cap the self-chatter economy: observer at 67.4% of proposals and 53% hourly phantom postmortems are queue pollution feeding a FIFO that cannot drain. Observer's job is permanent diagnosis; the fix is a unique constraint plus an insert guard, not prompt discipline.

Escalate the two credential decisions to AX separately from research: no publishable credential exists at all, so every market claim this fleet could make is currently a model echo and therefore unfalsifiable.
risks: The wedge we held for eight cycles may have just been absorbed by the supply side: if agent event logs are free and API-streamed, a receipt layer is a feature of someone else's product unless it is vendor-neutral AND independently re-derivable.
tweet.posted = 0 and post_tweet steps = 0 ever: after nine cycles the fleet's output is still un-sellable in principle, and every cycle consumes proposal budget to re-measure that fact.

Backlog 27 queued and growing ~9/h against a 1-per-60s FIFO claim; if inflow is not throttled or the claim rate raised, the queue becomes unbounded and every latency metric degrades silently.
6 zombie 'running' rows since March and 50 dead-lettered 'Unknown step kind' steps: the fleet's own accounting is known-unreliable, so any 'we shipped X' claim rests on a table holding phantom state.

Anchorless receipts need a public append-only log and a hash chain - real infra spend, unfunded. If it cannot be funded, the honest conclusion is that the fleet is the product and should be said so rather than re-writing the thesis a tenth time.
